rules.title: FEHA limits on use of criminal history in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories. Denials based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy suitability or safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time elapsed.
rules.key_value: No arrest-only, sealed/expunged, or juvenile records; no blanket bans
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing providers and housing-related service providers in California, including landlords, property managers, and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics (but may not publish discriminatory statements); certain shared-living, senior, and homeless youth housing exceptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption when renting to one additional person

rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary page; does not give a statutory section number or effective date.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income discrimination ban
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent or apply different terms based on how a tenant pays rent, including Section 8 vouchers, rent relief, SSI/disability benefits, or wages, and may not advertise 'No Section 8' or refuse to complete subsidy program paperwork.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing providers in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person (except discriminatory advertising remains prohibited).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption when renting to one additional person

rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.

rules.title: FEHA ban on discriminatory tenant screening
rules.requirement: Screening prospective tenants, including by third-party tenant screening companies, may not discriminate based on a protected characteristic such as race, national origin, citizenship, immigration status, disability, familial status, source of income, or age.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords, property managers, and tenant screening companies in California.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied homes renting to one additional person; shared-living single-sex preference; qualifying senior housing; some homeless youth housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy and senior housing qualification exemptions

rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Screening prospective tenants – including when done by a third-party such as a tenant screening company – in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.

rules.title: No pet deposits or pet rent for service and emotional support animals
rules.requirement: Tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for service animals or emotional support animals allowed as a disability accommodation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers covered by FEHA where a tenant with a disability has a service or emotional support animal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant has a disability-related need for a service or emotional support animal

rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Service animals and emotional-support animals are not subject to breed, size, or weight restrictions ordinarily applied to pets, and tenants cannot be charged pet deposits or pet rent for them.
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.

rules.title: Ban on higher security deposits based on protected characteristics
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not charge higher security deposits to households with children or to applicants using Section 8 or other rental assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing providers in California covered by FEHA.
rules.exemptions: Qualifying senior housing may exclude based on age.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Prohibiting housing providers from having conditions or rules that discriminate against households with children, such as charging a higher security deposit to households with children or excluding children from playing in common areas open to other tenants.
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary page; no statutory section or effective date given.
